Draw a diamond of letters from `A` out to a given letter and back.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/diamond) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: diamond.nomi
//# Draws a diamond of letters from `A` to a given letter and back.

/// The rows of a diamond of letters from `A` to `widest` and back, each
/// padded with spaces to the diamond's width. `widest` is an uppercase
/// ASCII letter.
pub fn rows(widest: Codepoint) -> List<String> {
    letters = Iter.to_list('A'..=widest)
    size = Iter.count(letters)

    top =
        letters
        |> Iter.with_index()
        |> Iter.map(fn #(i, letter) -> row(letter, i, size))
        |> Iter.to_list()

    bottom = top |> Iter.reverse() |> Iter.drop(1)
    [..top, ..bottom]
}

/// Row `i` of a diamond `size` letters tall to its middle, holding `letter`.
fn row(letter: Codepoint, i: Int, size: Int) -> String {
    outside = String.repeat(" ", size - 1 - i)

    if i == 0 {
        "${outside}${letter}${outside}"
    } else {
        inside = String.repeat(" ", 2 * i - 1)
        "${outside}${letter}${inside}${letter}${outside}"
    }
}

// FILE: diamond_test.nomi
import diamond

test "Degenerate case with a single 'A' row" {
    assert diamond.rows('A') == [
        "A",
    ]
}

test "Degenerate case with no row containing 3 distinct groups of spaces" {
    assert diamond.rows('B') == [
        " A ",
        "B B",
        " A ",
    ]
}

test "Smallest non-degenerate case with odd diamond side length" {
    assert diamond.rows('C') == [
        "  A  ",
        " B B ",
        "C   C",
        " B B ",
        "  A  ",
    ]
}

test "Smallest non-degenerate case with even diamond side length" {
    assert diamond.rows('D') == [
        "   A   ",
        "  B B  ",
        " C   C ",
        "D     D",
        " C   C ",
        "  B B  ",
        "   A   ",
    ]
}

test "Largest possible diamond" {
    assert diamond.rows('Z') == [
        "                         A                         ",
        "                        B B                        ",
        "                       C   C                       ",
        "                      D     D                      ",
        "                     E       E                     ",
        "                    F         F                    ",
        "                   G           G                   ",
        "                  H             H                  ",
        "                 I               I                 ",
        "                J                 J                ",
        "               K                   K               ",
        "              L                     L              ",
        "             M                       M             ",
        "            N                         N            ",
        "           O                           O           ",
        "          P                             P          ",
        "         Q                               Q         ",
        "        R                                 R        ",
        "       S                                   S       ",
        "      T                                     T      ",
        "     U                                       U     ",
        "    V                                         V    ",
        "   W                                           W   ",
        "  X                                             X  ",
        " Y                                               Y ",
        "Z                                                 Z",
        " Y                                               Y ",
        "  X                                             X  ",
        "   W                                           W   ",
        "    V                                         V    ",
        "     U                                       U     ",
        "      T                                     T      ",
        "       S                                   S       ",
        "        R                                 R        ",
        "         Q                               Q         ",
        "          P                             P          ",
        "           O                           O           ",
        "            N                         N            ",
        "             M                       M             ",
        "              L                     L              ",
        "               K                   K               ",
        "                J                 J                ",
        "                 I               I                 ",
        "                  H             H                  ",
        "                   G           G                   ",
        "                    F         F                    ",

```

## How it's written

- `rows` takes the widest letter as a `Codepoint`, so `'A'..=widest` is the list of letters with no conversion. The canonical input is a one-letter string; `'C'` says the same and cannot be two letters.
- The top half is built row by row from `Iter.with_index`, and the bottom half is the top reversed without its last row, joined as `[..top, ..bottom]`.
- `row` pads with `String.repeat`. The first row is its own branch, since it holds one letter rather than two.
- The five cases are plain `test` blocks rather than a `subtests` table. Each expected value is a list of up to 51 rows, which reads better under its own test name than as a table row.
